interpretation: This file maps every resource and data source registered by the pinned provider in this cohort. Fixture inclusion is not proof of a working lifecycle or complete AWS behavior. Unsupported and unexercised settings are separate.
requirements: Rebuilt bin/stackd with the SNS feedback admission change
Unchanged AWS provider 6.68.0 and its retained package hashes
Unused loopback port 14702; no engine containers are required
planned_lifecycle: Create all configured resource instances and read every included data source
Consume SNS to SQS, reject an unmatched subscription revision, and use actual topic and queue policies
Consume EventBridge rule and input-path targets through SQS and authenticated HTTPS, and observe actual archive admission
Consume SQS source records through Pipes input transformation and prove source acknowledgment
Deploy immutable hosted AppConfig bytes, read them through AppConfig Data, reject a consumed token, read a zero-byte no-change result, and consume the real completion extension
Advance shared service time through three Scheduler occurrences, revoke current role permission after admission, consume a real DLQ failure, restore authority, and consume a later occurrence
Stop Pipes, consume three actual SQS visibility receipts, prove policy-driven movement to the DLQ, and restart Pipes
Refresh and require a detailed-exitcode zero no-change plan; apply the saved plan

Remove and import every cohort resource into the same private state; derive SQS HTTPS import identity from signed native QueueArn and botocore endpoint metadata while provider transport remains the explicit loopback endpoint; reapply the write-only Connection API key, then require a no-change plan

Update resource descriptions, tags, filters, schedules and hosted configuration to v2; repeat real consumer and no-change checks; gracefully reopen the SQLite controller with unchanged service time and repeat real consumers without replaying an AppConfig extension notification

Destroy ordinary resources through a deletion-only saved plan, check only the service-linked role remains, advance owned service time by its configured maximum session duration plus one second, then apply the final ordinary deletion-only plan; verify native owner absence and empty Terraform state
A semantic no-op Terraform Core detailed-exitcode 2 remains a terminal strict failure, but does not skip independent import/update/reopen or cleanup evidence

iam_prerequisites.note: The four execution roles have native service trust and scoped permissions. Root provisioning enters normal PassRole admission. The EventBridge service-linked role is explicitly Terraform-owned. Ordinary resources, including Connection and its managed secret, are destroyed first; the runner preserves the active-session deletion guard and advances only its owned manual time beyond the configured session bound before final ordinary destruction. Prerequisite IAM resources are not part of this cohort's import loop.

baseline_diagnosis.controller: Existing bin/stackd; not rebuilt by the worker
baseline_diagnosis.result: Ordinary apply failed at SNS SetTopicAttributes(ApplicationSuccessFeedbackSampleRate=0). The provider's unset Optional integer sends zero on create.
baseline_diagnosis.cleanup: The finally block ran ordinary Terraform destroy; Terraform reported 37 destroyed resources. No real consumer checks ran because apply failed. Signed final absence was not checked in this failed run.
baseline_diagnosis.fix: Use the existing typed feedback map for the independent valid application sample rate and empty role clearing. Keep nonempty mobile feedback roles and mobile delivery unsupported. The normal resource transaction, IAM authorization and API events are unchanged.

revision_one_consumers_completed: SNS to SQS with filter and policies
EventBridge queue and authenticated HTTPS targets with archive admission
AppConfig bytes, token/no-change polling and extension delivery
Scheduler timing, current-role denial, DLQ and recovery
Actual SQS redrive and Pipes stop/start
parent_runtime_diagnosis.lifecycle_result: Stopped at the Create no-change plan. The only planned resource mutation was the omitted service-linked-role description changing the native default to null.
parent_runtime_diagnosis.destroy_result: Failed on the provider's SNS default policy containing legacy SNS:Receive and on a Connection deletion deadline while manual service time was paused.
focused_fixes: Native-calibrated legacy SNS:Receive topic-policy admission, without a Receive API or broad unknown-action admission
Advance service time only while a real Connection is in an asynchronous transition during mutating Terraform operations; fence controlled future Scheduler deadlines
Preserve parent-added state backup/restore around failed imports

native_policy_calibration.cleanup: DeleteTopic succeeded and GetTopicAttributes returned NotFound

import_and_transport_contract.identity: Signed GetQueueAttributes supplies the actual QueueArn; botocore endpoint metadata supplies the partition-correct HTTPS SQS hostname. Queue, queue policy and both redrive resources use that identity.
import_and_transport_contract.transport: main.tf keeps sqs = var.endpoint. The pinned provider service_package_gen.go passes that endpoint to withBaseEndpoint; service_endpoint_resolver_gen.go resolves the explicit endpoint before AWS defaults. The QueueUrl is request identity, not transport routing.
import_and_transport_contract.discovery: Compare signed authoritative queue identities, not loopback URL spelling against provider canonical import spelling.

retained_cleanup.result: Both reopened normally, destroyed remaining ordinary resources before the service-linked role, advanced only owned manual service time by configured MaxSessionDuration plus one second, and finished ordinary Terraform destroy with empty state and signed NoSuchEntity role reads.

reopen_notification_diagnosis.passed: All 37 non-IAM resource-instance imports, v1/v2 real consumers and Create/Import/Update detailed-exitcode zero plans. Reopened SNS/EventBridge HTTPS/Pipes consumers also passed.
reopen_notification_diagnosis.failure: The first reopen attempt incorrectly waited for a second AppConfig completion extension after an unchanged completed deployment. The notification was already acknowledged before restart.
reopen_notification_diagnosis.fix: Reopen still verifies deployed bytes, single-use tokens and no-change polling, but now asserts that the completed deployment notification is not replayed.
reopen_notification_diagnosis.cleanup: Normal saved plans destroyed 45 ordinary resources, then one service-linked role after 3601 seconds of owned service-time advancement. A separate signed owner check confirmed all named native resources absent and Terraform state empty.

completed_lifecycle.result: Exit 0 after 567.45 seconds. All configured create/import/update/reopen/current-IAM real-consumer assertions and strict zero-exit no-change plans completed; normal two-stage Terraform teardown, signed owner absence and empty state assertions completed.

completed_lifecycle.transport_evidence: import-provider.log contains 722 http.url values, all at 127.0.0.1:14802, and 18 request bodies using canonical HTTPS SQS QueueUrl identities. No logged import request used an AWS transport endpoint.
completed_lifecycle.artifact_limitation: The background-tool success result retained only the first 1524 stdout lines; the missing later output was reported as a tool issue. The successful process result, private provider import log, retained plans and empty final state remain evidence. This is configured-fixture coverage, not a claim about unsupported settings.
